answer: A seat is one apiary stand. The applicant files coordinates and twelve hive tags; each month an officer takes a mite wash from four hives and a dawn flight count, and the node reads those against the stand's daily scale weight, refusing tags that show at another site and any stand within three kilometres of a live one, since foragers wander that far and no farther. Hives run 180 dollars, twelve to a stand, scale 400, registration 260: near 2,800 a clone, 18 months before comb. A hollow log holds bees anywhere; only the weighed stand counts at dawn, so fifty clones clear 140,000 dollars.
